name: DensoDB
tagline: Small .NET document store from 2012 that ran in-process, as a Windows service, or as a P2P-synced mesh.
description: DensoDB (styled DeNSo DB) was an open-source document database for .NET written in C# by Paolo Possanzini and hosted on CodePlex, later mirrored to GitHub. Entities were serialised into BSON-like documents in schema-free collections keyed by a unique id, and queried with LINQ. It could run in-process for speed, as a Windows service exposing REST and WCF endpoints, or as a peer-to-peer mesh in which nodes synchronised and propagated events, and its internals were organised around CQRS with a journal and event-dispatcher plugins. The last CodePlex release dates from December 2012 and the GitHub mirror from 2013; LiteDB is the obvious modern replacement for embedded .NET document storage.
statusNote: Last release December 2012 and last commit October 2013; CodePlex has since shut down. LiteDB or RavenDB are the usual .NET successors.

scale.notes: Mesh mode replicated data between peers rather than sharding it.

strengths: Same API whether embedded in-process, run as a service or joined to a sync mesh
Stores plain .NET entities with built-in BSON serialisation and LINQ queries
CQRS-style event dispatcher made plugins such as P2P sync easy to bolt on
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 2013 and targets old .NET Framework and Windows Phone
GPLv2 licence is awkward for embedding in closed-source applications
No secondary indexes or documented consistency model for mesh sync
useCases: Historical reference for early embedded .NET NoSQL stores
Reading the code for a compact CQRS-based storage design
